issues.failure_explanation: The bilinear form depends only on gradients, so for the constant function $\varphi\equiv 1\in H^1(D)$ one has $a_{n,\theta}(1,1)=0$ while $\|1\|_{H^1(D)}^2=|D|>0$; hence $a_{n,\theta}$ is not coercive on $H^1(D)$ as stated. The statement omits the standard hypothesis needed here: homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions for the potential (the conditions actually imposed in the paper's computations) or passage to the quotient $H^1(D)/\mathbb R$. The unqualified well-posedness assertion of Corollary cor:added-1 inherits the same defect (existence up to the constant mode is consistent, since the right-hand side annihilates constants, but this is never stated).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the boundary conditions for the potential and formulate coercivity/well-posedness on $H^1_0(D)$ or on $H^1(D)/\mathbb R$ (equivalently, on the discretely Dirichlet-constrained space used in the numerics); the seminorm bound already proved in Proposition prop:boundedness then yields all conclusions, with uniqueness up to the constant mode.
issues.overall_effect: The coercivity claim of Lemma lem:added-1 is false as written, and the well-posedness of the discrete source update (Corollary cor:added-1) is unjustified until the potential space is constrained by boundary conditions or quotiented by constants.
issues.title: Coercivity claimed on all of H^1(D) despite the constant kernel
issues.why_classification: The repair is a standard local qualification already implicit in the paper's own computations; the method, all conclusions, and all rates survive unchanged once the potential space is constrained or quotiented.

issues.failure_explanation: For the constructed lumped product (trapezoidal/row-sum weights $m_{j,K}=\int_K\phi_{j,K}$), the lumped norm is not $O(h^s)$-close to the $L^2$ norm uniformly over $\mathbb V_h^d$: on affine quadrilateral cells take $\vec v_h$ whose nodal values are $\pm 1$ in a per-cell checkerboard pattern (a mapped $\mathbb Q_1$ field); then $\|\vec v_h\|_h^2=|D|$ while $\|\vec v_h\|_{\vec L^2(D)}^2=|D|/9$, i.e. $\|\vec v_h\|_h=3\|\vec v_h\|_{\vec L^2}$, an $O(1)$ relative gap at every mesh size $h$. Hence no shape-regular mesh family satisfies the assumption for the paper's lumped product: the hypothesis of Proposition prop:boundedness is vacuous for the scheme at hand, and its proof invokes the full-strength closeness (applied, moreover, to $\nabla\varphi_h$, which for the non-affine mappings the paper explicitly allows lies outside $\mathbb V_h^d$, hence outside the assumption's quantifier). The same false closeness is what justifies the $\mathcal O(h^{1+s})$ lumped-to-$L^2$ switch in Proposition prop:added-1.

failure_location.quote: \big|\|\vec v_h\|_h - \|\vec v_h\|_{\vec L^2(\domain)}\big| \;\le\; C\,h^s\,\|\vec v_h\|_{\vec L^2(\domain)} \quad\text{for all }\vec v_h\in\mathbb V_h^d.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the assumption as the standard uniform norm equivalence of the nodal lumped and $L^2$ norms on shape-regular $\mathbb Q_1$ mesh families, extended to the cellwise gradient fields $\nabla\mathbb H_h$; this restores Proposition prop:boundedness with the same form of constant. For the $\mathcal O(h^{1+s})$ switch in Proposition prop:added-1, add a standard quadrature-error (Bramble-Hilbert, exactness on $\mathbb Q_1$) estimate for the nodal quadrature applied to the smooth fields involved, which yields the rate with $s\le 1$.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition prop:boundedness as stated quantifies over an empty hypothesis class for the actual scheme, and the $\mathcal O(h^{1+s})$ quadrature-switch rate feeding Proposition prop:added-1 and Corollary cor:added-3 is supported only by a premise that cannot hold.
issues.title: Uniform O(h^s) closeness of lumped and L^2 norms is unsatisfiable for the nodal Q1 lumping
issues.why_classification: The stated assumption is impossible for the paper's lumped product, so it must be replaced rather than merely supplemented; Proposition prop:boundedness is recovered routinely, but preserving the advertised $\mathcal O(h^{1+s)}$ rate requires a contained but nontrivial new quadrature-error lemma. No advertised result, regime, or rate is ultimately lost, so the issue is more than minor but not serious.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition prop:fully_discrete_parabolic_energy_balance proves an identity in which the increment (dissipation) term is multiplied by $(\theta-\tfrac12)$. Hence the total kinetic-plus-potential energy of the update decreases only for $\theta\ge\tfrac12$ and strictly increases for $\theta<\tfrac12$ whenever the state changes. The corollary asserts the $\le$ inequality for the update procedure with no restriction on $\theta$, so as stated it is false for $\theta<\tfrac12$; only the cases used in the paper ($\theta=\tfrac12$, equality, and $\theta=1$) are actually covered.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This can be achieved via an artificial relaxation approach by lowering the kinetic energy appropriately~\cite{eulerpoisson23}.

issues.failure_explanation: The rescaling factor $\{1-\max(0,\delta\mathcal E^{n+1}/\mathcal E^{n+1}_{\mathrm{kin}})\}^{1/2}$ is only real when $\delta\mathcal E^{n+1}\le\mathcal E^{n+1}_{\mathrm{kin}}$. Since $\delta\mathcal E^{n+1}$ can be positive and, per Corollary cor:added-3, can grow like $(t_n-t_0)\alpha\mathcal O(h+h^s)$, while the kinetic energy may be arbitrarily small or zero (e.g., a locally resting state), the regime $\delta\mathcal E^{n+1}>\mathcal E^{n+1}_{\mathrm{kin}}$ is legitimate and reachable: there the radicand is negative (or the ratio undefined at $\mathcal E^{n+1}_{\mathrm{kin}}=0$), so the update is ill-defined. Moreover, no rescaling of $\vec m$ can remove more kinetic energy than is present, so the advertised exact reestablishment of the discrete energy balance cannot be delivered by this device in that regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Guard the rescaling, e.g. $\vec m_i^{n+1}\leftarrow\{\max(0,\,1-\delta\mathcal E^{n+1}/\mathcal E^{n+1}_{\mathrm{kin}})\}^{1/2}\vec m_i^{n+1}$ with the ratio treated as $0$ when $\mathcal E^{n+1}_{\mathrm{kin}}=0$, and state that when $\delta\mathcal E^{n+1}>\mathcal E^{n+1}_{\mathrm{kin}}$ only partial compensation is possible, so the post-restart energy balance degrades to an inequality in that degenerate regime.
issues.overall_effect: The Gauß-law-restart-with-relaxation post-processing is undefined in the depleted-kinetic-energy regime and its stated purpose—restoring the discrete energy balance after the restart—fails there; outside that regime the construction works as described.
issues.title: Energy-relaxation momentum rescaling is ill-defined when the potential-energy jump exceeds the kinetic energy
issues.why_classification: A one-line clamp makes the procedure well-defined and preserves the exact energy-balance restoration whenever the kinetic energy suffices to compensate; the only loss occurs in the degenerate regime $\delta\mathcal E^{n+1}>\mathcal E^{n+1}_{\mathrm{kin}}$, where exact compensation is impossible in principle, so the repair is a local degenerate-case fix.
